citation_entries.sentence: Among us the turning of a life came at baptism, and people called being baptized being enlightened.
The light of baptism was new birth spoken of as new sight.
We did not take baptism for a ceremony announcing a choice already made.
We held it to be a real crossing, in the body, into the new life.
It was not a private mystical experience, and it belonged to the community's own worship.
The way to the water was long: katechesis, the staged and tested teaching given over a long time to those preparing for baptism.
The baptized did not come up from the water already fully formed.
Formation went on as a real turning of the whole person toward a share in the divine life, step by step.

text: Among us the turning of a life came at baptism, and people called being baptized being enlightened. The light of baptism was new birth spoken of as new sight. We did not take baptism for a ceremony announcing a choice already made. We held it to be a real crossing, in the body, into the new life. It was not a private mystical experience, and it belonged to the community's own worship. The way to the water was long: katechesis, the staged and tested teaching given over a long time to those preparing for baptism. The baptized did not come up from the water already fully formed. Formation went on as a real turning of the whole person toward a share in the divine life, step by step.
